h1: The 6 Best Cordless Lawn Mowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Cordless Lawn Mowers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six cordless lawn mowers from 16 to 21 inch decks, covering voltage, battery count, drive type and the lawns each suits.
summary: The EGO Power+ LM2114 is the best cordless mower here, with a full 21 inch deck, a 56V platform and the battery in the box. Slopes call for the self-propelled Greenworks 80V. If you want a whole-yard kit, the Greenworks 48V combo bundles a mower, trimmer and blower, and the SEYVUM is the cheap small-lawn pick.
intro: Voltage sells cordless mowers, but amp-hours decide how much grass you cut. A 40V machine carrying a big battery can outlast a 56V one with a small pack, and a second battery lets you finish the back lawn while the first one charges. The label on the box tells you far less than the battery spec beside it.

We ranked six mowers from their listings, looking at deck width, battery arrangement, drive type and bundled tools. Battery numbers and owner notes shaped the order, and prices are shown as buckets only. Mowing time swings with grass height and terrain, so treat any runtime claim as a rough guide.

products.name: EGO Power+ 21-Inch Cordless Lawn Mower (LM2114)
products.verdict: A full-width cordless deck with battery and charger in the box.
products.description:
The EGO Power+ LM2114 is a push mower with a 21 inch deck on EGO's 56V battery platform. The battery and charger come in the box, and there is no gas or cord to manage. It sits in the $200 to $500 bucket.

It leads because it combines a full-width deck with a strong platform and no add-on purchases. The Greenworks 80V just below adds drive wheels for hills, but EGO's larger battery family gives it more room to grow if you later buy a trimmer or blower. A full deck also means fewer passes across the lawn.

Buy it for a standard, mostly flat yard where you are happy to push. The caveat is that there is no drive assist, so slopes and long grass will make it a workout.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Self-Propelled Mower
products.verdict: Drive wheels cut the walking effort on bigger lawns.
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V is a 21 inch self-propelled mower running on an 80V 4Ah battery, with the battery and charger included. It sits in the same $200 to $500 bucket as the EGO.

Second place reflects a trade. Self-propelled drive removes much of the walking effort on large or sloped yards, an edge the EGO cannot match. But the EGO sits on a bigger battery family, and a single 4Ah pack may run short on properties past mid-size.

Buy it if your lawn has hills or you dislike pushing a heavy deck. Skip it if the lawn is small and flat, since you would pay for drive you hardly use. Budget for a second battery if your yard tests the first one.
products.skipIf: Your lawn is small and flat.

products.name: Greenworks 48V (24V x 2) 20-Inch Mower, Trimmer, and Blower Combo Kit
products.verdict: Mower, trimmer and blower on one battery system.
products.description:
Greenworks' 48V kit is a 20 inch mower on a 24V by 2 battery bay, bundled with a string trimmer and a 320 CFM blower. Three batteries and chargers come in the box. It lives in the $500 and up bucket.

It ranks third because the price is the highest here and the mower deck is a step below the EGO. The case for it is consolidation: one purchase replaces three separate tools, and every battery fits across them.

Buy it if you are outfitting a whole yard from scratch and want a single battery system. The caveat is cost, because anyone who only needs a mower can spend far less on the EGO or the Greenworks 80V and add tools later.
products.idealFor: Outfitting a whole yard at once.

products.name: SEYVUM 40V 16-Inch Cordless Lawn Mower
products.verdict: Two batteries and a 45L bag for less money.
products.description:
The SEYVUM is a 16 inch push mower on a 40V platform that ships with two 4Ah batteries and a 45L collection bag. It sits in the $100 to $200 bucket and has a lightweight design.

It holds fourth place because a spare battery is a real advantage over the Greenworks 40V below, which supplies one, and it costs less. What holds it back is the narrow 16 inch deck, which means more passes and a poor fit for larger lawns.

Buy it for a small yard where you value long sessions and a low price. Skip it if your lawn is mid-size, as the wider EGO and Greenworks 80V cut far more per pass. The collection bag helps small yards stay tidy.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 16-Inch Cordless Push Mower
products.verdict: A compact mower that shares batteries with Greenworks 40V tools.
products.description:
The Greenworks 40V is a compact 16 inch push mower with a 40V 4Ah battery and charger included. It lands in the $200 to $500 bucket. Its batteries fit other Greenworks 40V tools.

It ranks fifth because the SEYVUM gives you two batteries for less money. This model is justified by compatibility: if you already own Greenworks 40V gear, the battery is shared, and that saves real cash against buying a separate platform.

Buy it for a small lawn and a Greenworks tool collection. Skip it if you want a spare battery in the box, or if you are shopping purely on price, because the SEYVUM undercuts it on both counts. For newcomers to the brand, the price exceeds what the size suggests.
products.skipIf: You want a spare battery included.

products.name: 18-Inch 40V Brushless Cordless Push Lawn Mower
products.verdict: A wide brushless deck at the lowest entry price.
products.description:
This 18 inch push mower uses a 40V brushless motor in a lightweight frame. It sits in the $100 to $200 bucket, giving it a wider cut than the 16 inch models above it.

It ranks last because the listing provides no battery details. Without amp-hours, runtime is a guess, and a mower is only as good as its pack. The brushless motor and wider deck are the draws, but an unclear listing is a risk, and replacement packs may be harder to source later.

Buy it if the lowest cost is the goal and you have a small yard. Skip it if you want confirmed battery specs, in which case the SEYVUM, with two 4Ah batteries stated outright, is a safer choice.

whatMatters.detail: Ah, or amp-hours, measures how much charge a battery holds, so a higher number means more mowing per charge. Voltage alone does not tell you runtime. Compare Ah figures across listings, and confirm that a battery is included. A listing that names no Ah value, as the 18 inch model does, deserves caution.

Voltage indicates the power class and, more usefully, which tools share the battery. Batteries generally fit only one brand's platform. This matters because a shared platform lets you add a trimmer or blower for the price of a bare tool. Check what else you own, and read the voltage in the title.

Deck width is the cutting path per pass. A 16 inch deck suits small lawns, while a 21 inch deck is the standard for typical yards, and wider decks mean fewer passes. Find the inch figure in the title. Match it to your lawn, remembering that a wide deck is harder to store and maneuver.

Self-propelled mowers drive their own wheels, so you steer instead of push. They help on slopes and larger lawns, and they weigh more. The Greenworks 80V is the only self-propelled model here. Check the drive wording in the listing, because push-only models say so plainly.

A spare battery lets you keep mowing while the first one charges, doubling your session. Some kits supply extras, such as the SEYVUM with two and the Greenworks combo with three. Read the box contents on the listing, and see whether extra packs are sold separately for your platform.

faq.q: How long does a cordless mower run?
faq.a: It depends on battery capacity, grass height and terrain, so treat any listed minutes as a guide. A spare pack is the simplest fix, and the SEYVUM includes two 4Ah batteries.
Comparing voltage alone. The Greenworks 80V and the EGO 56V sound very different, but amp-hours decide how long you mow. Read the Ah figure, and check whether the battery is included.

faq.q: Is the Greenworks 80V worth it over the EGO?
faq.a: Yes, if you have slopes or a larger lawn and want drive wheels. For a flat, standard yard, the push-only EGO Power+ LM2114 covers the same 21 inch deck for less effort in setup and cost.

Within the same brand and voltage platform, often yes. A Greenworks 40V mower shares batteries with Greenworks 40V tools, and the combo kit shares its 24V packs across all three tools. Never mix brands.

faq.q: How do I store the battery?
faq.a: Store the battery at a moderate temperature and not fully drained. Keep EGO and Greenworks packs indoors in winter, off the charger once full, and wipe the deck clean before storing the mower.

faq.q: Do cordless mowers handle wet grass?
faq.a: They struggle. Wet grass clumps under the deck and drains a battery quickly, even on an EGO Power+ LM2114. Mow when the lawn is dry, and cut a little at a time if the grass is tall.

finalTake: For a flat, standard lawn, the EGO Power+ LM2114 is the easiest recommendation. Hills push you toward the self-propelled Greenworks 80V, and small yards can save with the SEYVUM and its two batteries. Buy into the Greenworks combo kit only when you need a trimmer and blower as well, and verify battery details on the budget 18 inch model.
